vrcamera.message.seated: Camera: not available in seated mode
vrcamera.config.title: VR Camera
vrcamera.config.presets.description: Shots placed by hand. Grab the camera in VR to place the active one, add and delete them in the pause menu.
vrcamera.option.forceMirror.tooltip: Shows the camera view in the game window while the camera is on. Applies the next time the camera is turned on.
vrcamera.option.marker.tooltip: What shows where the camera is, in the headset. Never visible in the recording.
vrcamera.option.markerLabel.tooltip: Shows the name of the current shot next to the dot.
vrcamera.option.debugOverlay.tooltip: Shows what the camera is doing and why, on the HUD.
vrcamera.option.aimHeight.tooltip: Where on the body the camera aims. 0 is the feet, 1 is the head.
vrcamera.option.positionLag.tooltip: How long the camera takes to reach its position. Higher is smoother and slower.
vrcamera.option.lookLag.tooltip: How long the camera aim takes to catch up with the player.
vrcamera.option.turnLag.tooltip: How long the camera takes to swing around when the player turns.
vrcamera.option.turnDeadzone.tooltip: How far the player can turn before the camera starts to move. Raise this if the camera swings around too much.
vrcamera.option.leadRoom.tooltip: Aims ahead of a moving player, to leave room in the frame where they are going. 0 aims exactly at the body.
vrcamera.option.leadRoomMax.tooltip: Most the aim moves away from the player, in player sizes.
vrcamera.option.orbitSpeed.tooltip: How fast the orbit shot circles the player.
vrcamera.option.speedFov.tooltip: Widens the view at high speeds.
vrcamera.option.collisionRadius.tooltip: How far the camera stays away from blocks.
vrcamera.option.collisionMargin.tooltip: Additional distance to a block that is in the way.
vrcamera.option.softOcclusionTime.toolti: How long the camera ignores something thin between it and the player, like a tree. 0 turns this off.
vrcamera.option.occlusionRatio.tooltip: The shot is replaced when walls push the camera closer than this part of its distance.
vrcamera.option.occlusionCutTime.tooltip: How long the camera has to be squeezed before the shot is replaced.
vrcamera.option.transition.tooltip: How the camera gets to the next shot. Cut jumps there, swing flies around the player.
vrcamera.option.blendChance.tooltip: Chance for a swing instead of a cut, with automatic transitions.
vrcamera.option.minShotTime.tooltip: A shot stays at least this long, before it is replaced because the situation changed.
vrcamera.option.manualHoldSeconds.toolti: How long the director keeps a camera that was placed by hand.
vrcamera.option.events.tooltip: Special shots for dying and for long falls.
vrcamera.option.customInRotation.tooltip: The director also picks the hand placed shots.
vrcamera.shot.field.enabled.tooltip: If the director may use this shot.
vrcamera.shot.field.weight.tooltip: How often this shot is picked, compared to the others.
vrcamera.shot.field.azimuth.tooltip: 0 is in front of the player, 180 is behind.
vrcamera.shot.field.elevation.tooltip: How high above the horizon the camera is, seen from the player.
vrcamera.shot.field.distance.tooltip: In blocks for a regular sized player.
vrcamera.shot.field.fov.tooltip: Field of view of the camera.
vrcamera.shot.field.minDuration.tooltip: The shot stays at least this long.
vrcamera.shot.field.maxDuration.tooltip: The shot stays at most this long.
vrcamera.shot.shoulder.tooltip: Behind the player, looking over their shoulder.
vrcamera.shot.front.tooltip: In front of the player, backing away. Moves in while they stand still.
vrcamera.shot.flyby.tooltip: Stands ahead on the path and pans while the player passes. Distance is how far ahead, the angles are not used.
vrcamera.shot.crane.tooltip: Rises high up behind the player.
vrcamera.shot.duel.tooltip: Over the shoulder onto the opponent, both in frame. The angle around is measured from the opponent.
vrcamera.shot.death.tooltip: Circles the dead player. Only shown when dying.
vrcamera.shot.fall.tooltip: From above. Only shown on long falls.
vrcamera.message.summon: Camera: in front of you, grab it and place it
vrcamera.message.error: Camera: internal error, camera turned off (see log)
vrcamera.command.nocloth: Camera: the settings screen needs Cloth Config
vrcamera.command.nopreset: Camera: no such preset, active is %s
vrcamera.shot.pov.tooltip: Right in front of the face, looking where the player looks. Used where there is no room for a camera around the player. Distance is how far in front of the eyes, the angles are not used.
vrcamera.shot.menu.tooltip: Close over the shoulder onto an open menu: inventory, chest, pause menu. Only shown while one is open. The angle around is measured from the menu, lower it to see more past the shoulder.
vrcamera.option.indicator.tooltip: Shows a camera icon with the distance in the headset, where the camera is, also through walls. While the camera is out of sight the icon sticks to the edge of the view on that side. Never visible in the recording.
vrcamera.option.throwPower.tooltip: The camera can be grabbed and thrown, a faster throw goes further. This sets how far. 0 turns throwing off.
vrcamera.option.physicsAim.tooltip: In the physics mode: how much a dropped camera turns its lens to the player while it comes to rest. 0 leaves it lying however it fell, 1 makes it look right at the player.
vrcamera.option.indicatorSize.tooltip: Size of the camera icon and of the distance below it.
vrcamera.option.physicsShake.tooltip: In the physics mode: how much a camera held in the hand sways with breath and steps, and jolts when you get hurt. 0 keeps it as steady as the hand.
vrcamera.option.pullSeconds.tooltip: Look at the camera from afar, point a hand at it and hold the interact button. The controller buzzes harder and harder, and after this many seconds the camera flies into the hand. 0 turns pulling off.
vrcamera.option.pullAllModes.tooltip: Off: the camera can only be pulled in the physics mode. Turn it off if the hand catches the camera by accident while it films you from the front.
vrcamera.option.handStabilize.tooltip: Steadies a camera held in the hand: trembling and twitching of the hand, like while the other hand breaks a block, is smoothed out, moves that are meant still get through. 0 turns it off, higher is steadier but lags more behind the hand.
vrcamera.option.menuShotChat.tooltip: The director moves in close while the chat is open, like it does for an inventory. Turn it off if the cuts bother you when the chat is only open for a moment.
vrcamera.option.kickPower: Hit strength of hands and feet
vrcamera.option.kickPower.tooltip: In the physics mode: hands and feet hit a dropped camera, so it can be kicked or kept in the air like a volleyball. Feet need full body tracking. This sets how hard, 0 lets them pass through it.
vrcamera.option.hideHoldingArm: Hide the arm holding the camera
vrcamera.option.hideHoldingArm.tooltip: The arm that holds the camera is not drawn in the camera picture, it is right next to the lens. It stays visible when the camera looks at you, like in a selfie. Does not change what you see in the headset.
vrcamera.option.faceDistance: Aim at the face up close
vrcamera.option.faceDistance.tooltip: A camera closer to you than this many blocks aims at your face, one twice as far at your body, with a smooth change in between. Lets you put the camera right in front of you for a face shot. 0 always aims at the body.
vrcamera.option.underwaterLook.tooltip: In the physics mode: under water the camera films with a wider angle, sinks with a slow roll instead of tumbling, and leaves bubbles.
vrcamera.message.photo.off: Camera: turn the camera on to take a photo
vrcamera.option.photoSheet.tooltip: A photo you take slides out of the camera as a sheet of paper and falls to the ground. Pick it up like the camera, throw it, or let go of it at a block to pin it there. Pinned sheets are kept, the others are forgotten when you leave. Off: the photo is only saved to screenshots/vrcamera.
vrcamera.option.photoHoldSeconds.tooltip: How long the button of the photo gesture has to be held. The controller buzzes harder and harder until the shutter clicks. 0 takes the photo at once.
vrcamera.option.photoGesture.tooltip: How a photo is taken with a held camera. Same hand: hold the other button of the hand that holds the camera, the trigger while you grip it or the grip while you hold the trigger. Other hand: bring the other hand to the camera and hold its interact button. The key and /vrcam photo always work.
vrcamera.option.showOthersPhotos.tooltip: On servers with the VRCameraSync plugin, photos you pin are seen by everyone who has the mod, and you see theirs. Off: only your own are shown. Your photos are still shared.
vrcamera.message.pin.too_many: Camera: you have too many photos pinned on this server
vrcamera.message.pin.chunk_full: Camera: too many photos in this spot already
vrcamera.message.pin.too_fast: Camera: not so fast, pin it again in a moment
vrcamera.message.pin.refused: Camera: the server did not take this photo
vrcamera.option.shareCamera.tooltip: On servers with the VRCameraSync plugin, players with the mod within 32 blocks see your camera where it is, with your name over it. Off: nobody sees it. Photos you pin are shared either way.
vrcamera.option.showCustomPhotos.tooltip: Players can put pictures from the internet on sheets with /vrcam load. Those are not photos of the game and can show anything. Off: a black sheet stands in for them and the picture is not downloaded. Your own are always shown.
vrcamera.message.load.busy: Camera: wait, a picture is still loading
vrcamera.message.load.failed: Camera: could not load the picture: %s
vrcamera.message.load.done: Camera: picture loaded, it is in front of you
vrcamera.message.pin.not_allowed: Camera: this server does not let you do that
vrcamera.option.photoBrightness.tooltip: How much the picture on a sheet is brightened. A sheet is lit by the world around it and looks darker than the screen. 0 leaves it as taken. Applies to new photos, the saved file is not changed.
vrcamera.label.custom.hint: VR Camera settings → Show custom pictures of others
vrcamera.option.photoSounds.tooltip: The click of the shutter and the whirr of a sheet being printed, from your camera and from the cameras of others. Off mutes them for you. The others still hear your camera.
vrcamera.option.pace.tooltip: A ready-made set of shot lengths and camera calmness. Picking another one overwrites the lengths of the shots, the shortest shot time, the orbit speed and the turn settings, here and in the other tabs. They can be changed one by one after that.
vrcamera.option.photoPixels.tooltip: Turns the picture on a sheet into pixel art in the colours of a map of the game. 0 leaves it as taken, higher means fewer and larger pixels. Applies to new photos, the saved file is not changed.
vrcamera.option.selfieScreen.tooltip: While the camera is near you with its lens to you, a second screen stands on top of it and shows the picture, like a mirror. In your hand or wherever you put it. Only in the headset, not in the recording, and it costs no performance.
vrcamera.option.selfieDistance.tooltip: Up to how many blocks between your head and the camera the selfie screen is shown. Further away it is gone.
vrcamera.option.pullStyle.tooltip: Telekinesis: the camera comes to your hand for as long as you hold the button, follows the hand, and stays where it got to if you let go. In the physics mode it then flies on and falls. Instant: hold the button for the whole time, then it comes at once.
vrcamera.command.screen.vr: Camera: in VR the camera of Vivecraft does this, use the modes as usual
vrcamera.command.chroma.on: Camera: green screen on. Only entities are filmed, on one plain colour
vrcamera.option.attachToSelf.tooltip: The camera of the physics mode stays on your own head if you hold it there and let go slowly. Off: it only sticks to walls, mobs and other players.
vrcamera.option.chromaColor.tooltip: The colour behind the entities with /vrcam chroma on, as #RRGGBB. The usual green is #00B140, blue is #0047BB.
vrcamera.option.screenOutput.tooltip: Where the camera films to for a player without VR. Game window: in place of your own view. Own window: a second window for OBS, your own view stays as it is. That draws the world twice and costs FPS.
vrcamera.option.outputFps.tooltip: How many pictures per second the camera draws into its own window. Fewer cost less: the world is drawn a second time for each. 0 draws one with every frame of the game.
vrcamera.command.screen.window: Camera: it films into a window of its own now, your view stays yours
vrcamera.command.screen.screen: Camera: it films into the game window now
vrcamera.message.output.failed: Camera: its window could not be opened, it was turned off. See logs/latest.log
vrcamera.option.menuSize.tooltip: How large the screen with an open menu is that stands in front of your character for the camera. It shows the menu alone, whatever size that has in the game window.
vrcamera.option.chromaDistance.tooltip: With the green screen on, only entities this close to you are filmed, and only the ones the camera could see past the blocks of the world. 0 films all of them.
vrcamera.config.help: Hold Shift for what this does
vrcamera.message.steer.off: Camera: it works on its own again
vrcamera.option.cameraLabelDistance.tool: The other free cameras you put up are shown with their letter, and can be picked, up to this far away from you. 0 hides them all. The one that films has its icon in any case.
vrcamera.command.cam.none: There is no free camera %s here
vrcamera.option.othersCameras.tooltip: How many cameras of other players you see at once, the nearest ones. 0 shows none. Your own cameras are not counted.
